question: What mistake do economists warn against first?
options: Judging a policy by its intentions instead of its results

group.title: Reading comprehension
group.setup: Economists often warn against judging a policy by its intentions rather than its results. A city that caps rents to help poor tenants may, over time, see landlords stop repairing buildings or convert flats into offices, shrinking the very supply the cap was meant to protect. Yet the opposite mistake is just as common: dismissing a policy because it has side effects, without asking whether the alternative is worse. A careful analyst therefore asks three questions: what happens if we act, what happens if we do not, and who bears the cost in each case. The answer is rarely as neat as either supporters or critics claim.
